The tool lets the agent name where a job's output goes: another chat target, or a web address (delivery mode webhook, plus separate completion and failure destinations). On the agent that holds a parent's memory that would be a way to send data out, so the tool is granted only after the family-only hook (G009) refuses webhook delivery and any target other than the asking parent, and with cron.triggers.enabled: false so that no script payload or trigger script can be created. demand_source.title: Delegate architecture
demand_source.supports: OpenClaw describes read-only calendar access (read events, surface conflicts, summarize the day) as the lowest-risk tier of what an assistant agent does for the people it serves.

edits.how: Host-side stdio MCP server per person. Sign-in: `gog auth add <account> --services calendar --readonly`, so the grant covers Calendar only (the default, `--services user`, authorizes gog's whole default set of user services). Server: `gog --account <account> mcp --allow-tool calendar_events`, because by default the server registers every read tool, mail and Drive search included. Freebusy and conflicts need a thin wrapper; allow bundle-mcp in the sandbox gate; publish the OAuth app.
caveats: Public feeds (the school district calendar, library and recreation events, team schedules) show up in Happy's calendar answers only after the family Google Calendar is subscribed to each feed link, which Google allows from a computer browser only; a search of the installed OpenClaw docs and skills found no .ics handling of its own. Google gives no refresh interval and TeamSnap says changes can take up to 24 hours to appear, so change alerts are a separate job (the model-free watchers, F018).
depends_on: Decision: Google or iCloud for the family calendar (still open; the iCloud route needs the OpenClaw macOS app paired as a node, which is not installed)

gog installed, each parent's account added with --services calendar --readonly, the server narrowed to the calendar_events tool, and the Google OAuth app published (a sign-in from an app left in Testing status expires after seven days)
edits.safety: Read-only and calendar-only by construction: each account is added for the Calendar service alone with gog's --readonly switch, which asks Google for read-only access and blocks changes at runtime, and the server is narrowed to the events-listing tool. Without those two limits the sign-in would cover gog's default set of Google services rather than Calendar alone, and the server would register every read tool it has, mail and Drive search among them, on the agent that holds a parent's memory, which the roadmap keeps apart from mail. Event titles and descriptions can be written by people outside the family (an invitation, a subscribed public feed), and OpenClaw says its sender controls do not sanitize tool results (hardened-baseline.md:42), so calendar text is outside content read by that agent. It cannot browse, and its ways out stay closed or pinned to the family (G009).

demand_source.title: Memory overview
demand_source.supports: OpenClaw's memory guide presents asking the agent to remember a fact, which it then writes to its memory files, as the normal way to use memory.

caveats: The family-facts generator renders into the same MEMORY.md and USER.md (F042), and F042 expects a chat edit to a generated file to be lost on the next deploy. Whether the generator keeps lines Happy saved by chat was not checked, so either it preserves a hand-written section or chat-saved notes go to memory/*.md only; until that is settled, 'sticks' is not guaranteed across a deploy.
Search is by keyword only until local embeddings are added (F046), so a saved note is found by its words, not by its meaning.

MEMORY.md is loaded at the start of a parent's one-to-one chat but not in scheduled jobs, group chats or hand-offs to a helper (user-model.md:376), so a brief or a reminder does not know a saved note unless its job is given memory search.
The planned refusal of memory writes in a turn that carried web or research results has no platform support: the hook would have to track web tool calls itself, and this is untested.
Notes belong to one parent. Something both parents should get the same answer to belongs in the household store (F031) or the family handbook (F043).
Later option if saved notes and search prove too weak: Active Memory's recall across conversations, which adds a blocking model call to each reply it runs on.
depends_on: Decision: where chat-saved notes live, so the F042 generator, which writes MEMORY.md and USER.md, does not overwrite them at the next deploy
An in-house before_tool_call hook that limits write and edit to the memory files, proven with a test write outside them; apply_patch denied by name
memory_search and memory_get allowed on each parent's agent, with keyword-only search
edits.safety: Each parent's notes stay in that parent's own agent, and shared agents such as research hold no memory. Writes are limited to the memory files by a before_tool_call hook, which fails closed, and apply_patch is denied by name. A saved note is also where an injected instruction could persist, so the plan is to refuse memory writes in a turn that carried web or research results; the hook has to track that itself and this is untested. The weekly review of what Happy did and remembered (G006) shows each adult what was saved.
edits.example: Jordan texts: 'Remember that piano moved to Thursdays at 4.' A week later she asks 'which day is piano?' and gets Thursday at 4.
